development.summary: Add shared export controls to the three results pages
development.description:
Add the CSV, JSON and PDF choices to Matchup, Context and Model Metrics. Build each report from the displayed result and its filters.

Acceptance criteria:
- The three pages use one export control.
- Exports include the current result, context and limitations.
- Loading, empty and changed inputs prevent stale exports.

development.summary: Validate and deliver signed-in report downloads
development.description:
Add the bounded report formatter and same-origin download route for page snapshots.

Acceptance criteria:
- Validate the report kind, payload size and allowed role.
- Forward the signed-in session without putting tokens in download URLs.
- Return the correct filename and content type for CSV, JSON and PDF.
- Failed requests return an error, not a downloaded report.

development.summary: Test and deploy the shared export flow
development.description:
Run the export regression tests, deploy the change and download reports from all three pages.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compare exported values with the displayed results.
- Check stale results, retry, signed-out access and wrong roles.
- Record each test result and link any failure to its fix.
- Add screenshots of the working controls and readable downloads.

test_cases.summary: Matchup exports the displayed ranking in all three formats
test_cases.steps: Sign in as a coach. Select TOR against BOS, season 2024-25, and load a Matchup ranking. Export CSV, JSON and PDF. Open each file and compare its play types, scores, selected filters and ordering with the page.
test_cases.expected: All three files open and match the displayed ranking and selection. The report states its result scope.
test_cases.result: Pass; current execution and preserved failure history are in the Jira comments.

test_cases.summary: Context exports the selected situation and adjusted results
test_cases.steps: Sign in as a coach. Load Context with a supported matchup, change score margin and clock, then apply the context. Export CSV, JSON and PDF. Compare the result rows and context values with the page.
test_cases.expected: Each report contains the displayed adjusted results, the applied situation and its limitations. It does not replace them with a newly fetched baseline ranking.
test_cases.result: Pass; current execution and preserved failure history are in the Jira comments.

test_cases.summary: Model Metrics exports the visible evaluation results
test_cases.steps: Sign in as an analyst. Load Model Metrics with a supported season and evaluation settings. Export CSV, JSON and PDF after results appear. Compare the metric names, values, selected settings and limitations with the page.
test_cases.expected: The reports match the available evaluation results. Exporting does not start a new training or evaluation run.
test_cases.result: Pass; current execution and preserved failure history are in the Jira comments.

test_cases.summary: Export stays unavailable for empty, loading or stale results
test_cases.steps: On each export page, check the control before results load and while a request is pending. Load results, change a relevant input, then check the control before and after applying the change.
test_cases.expected: No report can be generated from empty, loading or stale results. Export becomes available when the displayed result matches the selection.
test_cases.result: Pass; current execution and preserved failure history are in the Jira comments.

test_cases.summary: Report downloads require the correct signed-in role
test_cases.steps: Request each report without a session. Repeat coach reports with an analyst account and the analyst metrics report with a coach account. Then repeat with the allowed account.
test_cases.expected: Signed-out requests return 401 and wrong-role requests return 403. Allowed requests return the report. Rejected requests do not return attachment headers or expose session tokens.
test_cases.result: Pass; current execution and preserved failure history are in the Jira comments.

test_cases.summary: Report validation rejects invalid and oversized snapshots
test_cases.steps: Send an unsupported report kind or format, malformed rows and a payload above the supported size limit. Send a valid small snapshot as a comparison.
test_cases.expected: Invalid requests return a clear client error and no attachment. The valid snapshot still downloads. There is no arbitrary backend URL or export path in the request contract.
test_cases.result: Pass; current execution and preserved failure history are in the Jira comments.

test_cases.summary: A failed report request shows an error and can be retried
test_cases.steps: Simulate a failed or unavailable report service after loading valid results. Click Export, inspect the message and file behavior, then restore the service and retry.
test_cases.expected: The control shows an understandable error, does not save the error body as a report, clears its busy state and permits a successful retry.
test_cases.result: Pass; current execution and preserved failure history are in the Jira comments.

test_cases.summary: Downloaded reports have readable filenames and content
test_cases.steps: Download CSV, JSON and PDF from each page. Inspect the filename, content type and actual file contents. Use a fixture with commas, quotes, line breaks and special characters in text values.
test_cases.expected: Each filename identifies the report and format. The content type matches a valid readable file. Text characters do not break CSV columns, JSON parsing or PDF rendering.
test_cases.result: Pass; current execution and preserved failure history are in the Jira comments.
